correctness.rationale: For the actual fixed-basis hypothesis on both C and D, the disjoint coordinate embeddings V,J give W=VC+JD with W*W=I and V*W=C. For column j the first possible index of W is 2 max(0,j−r)+2r+3>j; V advances support as well. Iteration into the coordinate tails proves purity, not just absence of eigenvectors. V has an infinite-dimensional orthogonal complement, and W does too: y↦−VD_*y+JC*y is isometric by D_*²+CC*=I and orthogonal to W by DC*=C*D_*, which follows by polynomial approximation of the square root. For the commutator step, the two-copy Y commutes with Z and satisfies Y²=I+4Z², so the block Q is idempotent and [P,Q] is the symmetric off-diagonal block with entries Z. Diagonalizing that block, alternating signs on wandering levels, and using Wold multiplicity give the asserted isometries and their scalar multiples as idempotent commutators; adjoint reverses the commutator order. Scaling then gives AB=T and AA*=B*B=sI, hence both norms are √s. This also handles the singular-defect boundary, with the zero case trivial. RESULT.md lines 18–36 supply the identities; CHECK.py and VERIFICATION.md were inspected, not executed. The reported 80 finite checks do not certify purity or endpoint attainment in infinite dimension.

value.rationale: Exact attainment is a meaningful distinction in an infinite-dimensional factorization problem already known with arbitrary positive slack. The basis-support construction handles familiar classes such as weighted shifts and diagonals with singular or nonclosed-range exact defects.
